overview.title: Money Function And Classification
overview.definition: Money is any universally accepted medium of exchange that standardizes value, acts as a deferred payment standard, and stores wealth over time. Its classification ranges from commodity and fiat money to narrow and broad money aggregates.
overview.importanceInUpsc: Frequently tested in UPSC Prelims regarding monetary aggregates (M1, M2, M3, M4), liquidity positions, and RBI's structural framework; highly relevant for Mains GS-3 (Indian Economy, Monetary Policy, and Inflation).
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of Money Function And Classification.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
prerequisites: Core foundational concepts of Barter System and Macroeconomics

sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Primary Functions of Money**: Serves as a **medium of exchange** (overcoming the double coincidence of wants) and a **unit of account / measure of value** (providing a common denominator for pricing goods).
• **Secondary Functions of Money**: Acts as a **standard of deferred payment** (facilitating credit and lending) and a **store of value** (preserving purchasing power over time).
• **Contingent Functions of Money**: Basis of credit creation, distribution of national income, measurement of marginal productivity, and increasing liquidity of capital.
• **Key Metric / Factor**: Liquidity continuum—ranging from most liquid currency in circulation to least liquid long-term time deposits.

sections.title: Comprehensive Classification & Comparative Matrix
rows: Has intrinsic value (e.g., gold, silver, salt coins). Used historically across global trade routes.
Market value of the commodity equals its face value as money.
Frequently tested in economic history and evolution of financial systems.
Inconvertible paper money made legal tender by government decree (e.g., modern INR notes and coins).
Backed by government trust and legal authority, not physical commodities.
Crucial for understanding Central Bank autonomy and RBI Act, 1934.
Accepted based on trust between payer and payee (e.g., cheques, drafts, bills of exchange).
Not legal tender; dependent on the creditworthiness of the issuer.
Important for distinguishing between statutory legal tender and commercial credit instruments.

items.definition: Money that law requires creditors to accept in discharge of debt. Divided into Limited Legal Tender (coins up to a certain limit under Coinage Act) and Unlimited Legal Tender (banknotes issued by RBI).
RBI's measures of money supply based on liquidity. M1 = Currency with public + Demand deposits with banks + Other deposits with RBI. M3 = M1 + Time deposits with banks (Broad Money).
Base money comprising currency in circulation, bankers' deposits with RBI, and other deposits with RBI. Controlled directly by the Central Bank.
Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 (Section 22 for note issuance), Coinage Act, 2011, and the Y.V. Reddy Working Group on Money Supply (1998).

items.title: Major Geographical Distribution / Regional Hubs
items.content:
• **Currency Printing Presses**: Security Printing and Minting Corporation of India Limited (SPMCIL) units at Nashik (Maharashtra) and Dewas (Dewas, MP); Bharatiya Reserve Bank Note Mudran Private Limited (BRBNMPL) presses at Mysuru (Karnataka) and Salboni (West Bengal).
• **Coin Mints**: Mumbai, Hyderabad, Kolkata, and Noida.

items.title: Challenges, Reforms & Forward Strategy
items.content:
• **Bottlenecks / Issues**: High cash-to-GDP ratio, counterfeit currency risks, and cost of fiat note management.
• **Policy Interventions**: Promotion of Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC / e-Rupee), Unified Payments Interface (UPI) expansion, and formalization of the economy.

items.title: Mnemonic for RBI Monetary Aggregates Liquidity Order
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym / Phrase**: "C D T T" (Currency, Demand, Time, Total-Post)
• **Decoded Meaning**: M1 = Currency + Demand deposits; M2 = M1 + Post Office savings; M3 = M1 + Time deposits; M4 = M3 + Total Post Office deposits.
• **Prelims Exam Value**: Instantly ranks monetary aggregates from most liquid (M1) to least liquid (M4).

items.title: Retention Rule of Thumb
items.content: • **Core Formula / Rule**: Reserve Money (M0) is the base multiplier engine; Broad Money (M3) is the most watched indicator for inflation and economic activity by RBI.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often frames statements claiming that Demand Deposits and Time Deposits are both part of Narrow Money (M1). Remember that Time Deposits are part of Broad Money (M3), never Narrow Money.

Mains Value Addition: Connect the evolution of money from physical fiat to CBDC (e-Rupee) as a structural leap in reducing printing costs, enhancing monetary policy transmission, and eliminating settlement risks.

keyTakeaways: Money fundamentally resolves the double coincidence of wants through its primary, secondary, and contingent functions.
Monetary aggregates are classified by liquidity, with M3 serving as the benchmark Broad Money indicator for macroeconomic planning.
Legal tender status must be distinguished from fiduciary money instruments like cheques and demand drafts.
